messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I’d be comfortable with a plan that gives each of us a fair financial share. If A buys the house, I won’t subsidize a family discount. My main worry is being pressured to give up my share—and damaging things with my twin over it.
My husband and I hope to buy the house at a family discount. I’d like us to find a way forward that C can agree to, without pressuring anyone.
I’d like to receive some money from the house to help me start a dance studio. A fair arrangement for all three of us matters, and I hope nobody feels pressured to give up their share.
I don’t know what the will says, and we haven’t settled on a price or how to calculate a discount.
I don’t have a copy, and I’m not sure who does. I don’t know what the will says about the house or our shares.
I don’t have a copy of the will, and I’m not sure who has it. I don’t have a specific amount or deadline for the studio money in mind yet.
Yes. I agree we should find the will and get an independent valuation, and make sure all three of us see the same information.

I’d consider a sale at an independent valuation, once we know what the will says and what each of our shares is. I won’t agree to a discount that reduces my share, and I want the terms shared with all three of us before anything is decided.

I’d be open to that, once we know what the will says, everyone’s shares, the independent valuation, and the proposed terms. I don’t know yet whether my payout would cover the studio, but I’m willing to help look for the will.
I’m willing to consider buying at the independent valuation, and to discuss a discount only from my own share once we know the will and shares. I’ll coordinate with B to help find the will.
I’ll wait until we’ve found and read the will together. Then we can get the valuation and review A’s written terms before anyone decides.
